prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you left the game at the start of the fourth quarter to beat traffic. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, members of the Committee—let me state clearly, unequivocally, and under penalty of losing my paper plate privileges:

I did not abandon the cookout game in the fourth quarter to “beat traffic.”

I stepped away briefly to check on the cooler, verify the structural integrity of the folding chairs, and ensure no unauthorized parties were double-dipping near the seven-layer dip. Any suggestion that I fled during crunch time is a gross mischaracterization of my movements and my commitment to the team, the grill, and this great nation’s potato salad.

Furthermore, I have witnesses who can confirm I was present for the decisive final minutes, standing near the fence, holding a hot dog, and offering strategic commentary such as “watch the screen” and “they gotta box out.”

I will not be smeared as a fair-weather fan. My record speaks for itself: I arrived before kickoff, contributed ice, respected the grillmaster’s authority, and remained until at least one uncle began explaining zone defense with condiment bottles.

So let the record show: I stayed. I cheered. I endured. And I did not, at any time, defect to the parking lot for the purpose of traffic avoidance.
